title: examples(streaming): update TS streaming snippets for current client API (async iteration, abort signals, final response)
author: Dana Lo
description:
Context: Our TS streaming examples drifted from the current SDK surface (we switched from the old EventEmitter-style callbacks to an async-iterable stream wrapper, and we now recommend AbortController for timeouts/cancellation). Support has also been seeing users miss the final response object (they only print deltas), leading to confusion around tool calls / final usage accounting.

This PR refreshes the canonical streaming examples to match the current client API and the event taxonomy we’re standardizing across SDKs.

What’s in this PR: (1) Replace legacy `client.chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` snippet with `client.responses.stream(...)` example using `for await (...)` iteration (2) Demonstrate cancellation/timeouts via AbortController (explicitly recommended for proxy/buffered networks) (3) Show how to capture and use the final response object after streaming completes (including guarding against early abort) (4) Add a small “disconnect / retry” note in the example README header (no reconnect implementation in SDK; just guidance) (5) Update the README snippets that docs-site links to, so they’re copy/paste runnable.

Example shape (illustrative): `const stream = await client.responses.stream({ model, input, signal: abort.signal }); for await (const event of stream) { if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta); } const final = await stream.finalResponse();`.

Notes: This PR is intentionally scoped to streaming only (tools + structured output examples are handled in #323/#324). I tried to keep naming consistent with the canonical patterns doc (token deltas vs final response), without renaming exported SDK types.

Checklist: - [x] Examples are runnable with minimal setup (REDWOOD_API_KEY) - [x] Uses safe patterns (no secret logging) - [x] Handles abort/cancel explicitly - [x] Prints deltas AND demonstrates final response capture - [x] Added/updated tests for snippet compilation/execution (mock server).

Refs: Linear ENG-2844 (TS examples refresh), ENG-2842 (canonical event model), SUP-18421 (stream disconnect reports behind corporate proxies).
commits: 1) examples: rewrite streaming quickstart to use async iteration 2) docs: update README streaming section + env var instructions 3) sdk: expose `finalResponse()` helper on stream wrapper (non-breaking) 4) tests: add snippet test for streaming example with mock server 5) chore: format + lint fixes for examples folder
changed_files:
High-level changes:
- examples/streaming/basic.ts (new): canonical streaming example using async iteration
- examples/streaming/abort-timeout.ts (new): abort controller + timeout pattern
- README.md: replace legacy streaming snippet; add note about final response capture
- src/streaming/ResponseStream.ts: add `finalResponse()` convenience + stronger typing for event iteration
- test/snippets/streaming.test.ts: run examples against mock server; assert final response presence
- package.json: add `test:snippets` script (wired into CI)

Small illustrative snippet (README):
`const abort = new AbortController(); const t = setTimeout(() => abort.abort(), 30_000); const stream = await client.responses.stream({ model: 'redwood/verified-llm', input: 'Write a haiku about latency.', signal: abort.signal }); try { for await (const event of stream) { if (event.type === 'response.output_text.delta') process.stdout.write(event.delta); } const final = await stream.finalResponse(); console.log('\n\nrequest_id:', final.request_id); } finally { clearTimeout(t); }`
conversation:
Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we be explicit about what users should do with the final response? The drift we saw was that people never call the finalizer and then they can’t find tool calls / usage.

Dana Lo (author): Yep — added a dedicated section in the README snippet: “Always capture final response for usage/tool calls”. Also added `finalResponse()` helper so it’s obvious.

Sabrina James (review): The delta event type string here should match the canonical taxonomy. I see `output_text.delta` in the loop but `message.delta` in abort-timeout.ts.

Dana Lo (author): Good catch. Normalized both examples to `response.output_text.delta` and updated comments. (This matches the canonical patterns draft and the docs PR language.)

Allison Grant (review): For abort guidance, can we call out that some proxies buffer responses and a longer timeout may be required? Also: please avoid recommending reconnect/resume as if it’s supported.

Dana Lo (author): Updated wording: we recommend AbortController + keepalive-friendly timeouts, and we explicitly say the SDK does not currently support resuming a partial stream; we suggest retrying idempotent requests when safe.

Elliot Price (review): Minor docs nit: ensure the env var naming matches docs-site (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and that the code block is copy/paste runnable.

Dana Lo (author): Updated and verified locally via `pnpm test:snippets`. Also added a one-liner about Node 18+.

Ibrahim Khan (final): Looks good. Thanks for adding the snippet test — this should prevent future drift.
